problem: Financial question answering is treated as ordinary document QA although evidence is multimodal and time-dependent: a disclosure may support a query only after it becomes public, so point-in-time validity must be enforced.
method: TempFinRAG: a multimodal temporal RAG framework that enforces the information boundary defined by SEC filing availability given a question, company and as-of date; aligns page layout, text, table structure and XBRL facts; retrieves time-valid evidence; executes auditable calculations; generates a cited answer; and verifies temporal validity, claim support, numerical consistency and abstention need.
key_assumptions: An as-of date is available per query
Evidence validity is determined by public availability (a hard temporal boundary), not graded recency
Crossmodal evidence should answer consistently (crossmodal evidence symmetry)
main_contribution: TempFinRAG plus the TempFinQA point-in-time evaluation protocol and a formalization of crossmodal evidence symmetry under a causal temporal boundary.
datasets: Public U.S. SEC filings and XBRL facts
benchmarks: Complementary evidence-grounded, numerical, conversational and multi-table benchmarks
results: On TempFinQA, answer accuracy improves from 66.7% to 78.9% over hybrid RAG, temporal evidence leakage falls from 10.8% to 1.7%, and hallucination falls from 17.3% to 7.9%.
limitations: Full text not open access; details beyond the abstract unknown
Financial filings rather than statutes/regulations; no near-duplicate amendment versions
Validity is modelled as a hard as-of availability boundary rather than a graded temporal relevance term

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: Enforces a hard 'as-of' information boundary derived from filing availability and adds a verifier, rather than adjusting a retriever's rank by elapsed time between query date and passage version; the corpus is multimodal financial filings, not overlapping amended legal versions, and it explicitly requires 'deliberately asymmetric access across time' instead of a symmetric graded decay.
relation_to_idea.basis: Abstract describes point-in-time retrieval with as-of date, temporal validity checking, and answer-accuracy/leakage metrics; it shares the problem framing and evaluation style but not the elapsed-time re-ranking mechanism or the amended-statute setting.
